name: First Embrace (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: small and premature newborns in public hospitals in Kano State, Nigeria.
summary: First Embrace runs kangaroo care, continuous skin-to-skin contact and breastfeeding support, for small and premature newborns on public hospital wards in Kano State, Nigeria, paying and training the nurses. In its first year, 2026, at two hospitals, it costs about {{row:cost_per_person}} per newborn enrolled; at the pilot hospital's own baseline about {{row:baseline_mortality_rate}} of these newborns died in their first month, and the 2026 Cochrane review finds kangaroo care cuts deaths by about {{row:mortality_reduction}}, counted only for the {{row:implementation_adj}} of newborns who get at least 2 hours a day. It comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 (plausible range {{range}}). The biggest uncertainties are the size of the effect at First Embrace's low daily dose and the baseline from 71 newborns; a randomised rollout across hospitals, which First Embrace plans, would settle both.

story.sentence: $1,000 pays for skin-to-skin care of small newborns in Kano, Nigeria. Every **{cost_per_person / (deaths_averted_per_person * total_adj)|$}** saves a newborn's life.

source.quote: 1,104 premature and underweight newborns cared for.

rows.explainer: Small (under 2.5 kg) and premature newborns enrolled since February 2026 (nurses log every session; the charity's own count): 1,104 by 18 November, plus the six weeks to the end of the year at about 250 a month (its reach and cost model: 254 in September and 214 so far in October at the two hospitals). rows.explainer: One: the mortality below is the risk over the whole neonatal period (28 days) of a newborn enrolled, not a yearly rate, and the care covers that period once.

The lost add about 1.9 deaths among those discharged alive and 2.0 among the rest, so the cohort's mortality is about {{row:cohort_mortality}}. A sample of 71 at one hospital in one month.

source.title: First Embrace, Introducing First Embrace: pilot results (29 July 2026)
source.quote: Baseline mortality among LBW newborns 17.9% 23.8% Calculated

rows.explainer: First Embrace's estimate for Kano by GiveWell's method: the state's neonatal mortality (59 per 1,000, NDHS 2023-24) × the share of neonatal deaths from low birthweight and prematurity (78.2%, GBD 2021) ÷ the share of births with low birthweight (19.4%, MICS 2016-17). Range 18% (the national figure, 17.9%) to 30% (the higher survey estimates of neonatal mortality).

source.title: First Embrace, Pilot baseline: how we measured neonatal mortality at the pilot hospital
source.quote: Those nine deaths come out of the numerator and the denominator alike, leaving 12 deaths among 71 newborns.

rows.explainer: Of the 21 baseline deaths, 9 were on day 0 or 1.

rows.label: All baseline deaths by day 28

source.title: First Embrace, Pilot baseline: how we measured neonatal mortality at the pilot hospital

rows.explainer: Known deaths among all 80 newborns followed.

rows.label: Kano reference, for newborns alive after day 1
rows.formula: kano_lbw_mortality * (1 - base_early_deaths / base_all_deaths) / (1 - kano_lbw_mortality * base_early_deaths / base_all_deaths)
rows.explainer: The Kano figure without the deaths on day 0 and 1, which the programme can't reach, at the baseline's own share of deaths that early (9 of 21): the risk for a newborn who survives the first two days.

rows.label: Weight on the hospital's own cohort
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (25 to 80%): the cohort is this hospital's own newborns, many referred in sick from elsewhere (40%), so it fits the programme better than a population figure; but it is 71 newborns in one month with a third lost to follow-up (its 95% interval for the naive count alone is 10% to 27%). First Embrace notes that the lost newborns' records make 'higher mortality estimates less plausible', and about 9% of its enrolled newborns die by day 28, both pulling below the loss-adjusted cohort figure.

rows.label: Deaths in the neonatal period among newborns the programme enrols, without it
rows.explainer: The hospital's loss-adjusted baseline and the Kano reference for newborns alive after day 1, weighted (Convention 7). A 28-day risk, not a yearly rate (years_of_coverage is one neonatal period).

rows.label: Relative risk of death with kangaroo care (any duration) against conventional care
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts/newborn_care.json): the 2026 Cochrane review, 0.81 (0.67 to 0.99), across the skin-to-skin durations hospitals deliver.

rows.label: Reduction in neonatal deaths with kangaroo care
rows.explainer: One minus the relative risk. First Embrace's own before-and-after data (about 9% dying after the programme began) would be a far larger fall, but the case mix differs and there is no comparison group: a check, not an effect.

rows.label: Indirect deaths per direct death (none: an all-cause effect)
rows.explainer: 0: the review's effect is on deaths from all causes, so no indirect deaths are added.

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Direct and indirect deaths over the years of protection. If the intervention protects several age groups with different risks, replace this formula with one row per group and sum them here; check the result against the all-cause trial result per person-year, scaled to today's mortality.

rows.label: Share of deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: All of the deaths averted are of newborns.

rows.label: Illness averted, as a share of the mortality and income benefits
rows.explainer: Illness averted (fewer infections and less hypothermia), as a share of the value of the deaths averted: the site's one figure for kangaroo care (facts/newborn_care.json, GiveWell's).

rows.label: Stillbirths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: 0: kangaroo care begins after birth and cannot avert stillbirths.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, ln(consumption) per year
rows.explainer: 0 here: survivors' later development is counted as a share of the deaths' value (developmental_share below), as the site's one figure for kangaroo care has it, not as a separate income gain.

rows.label: Years until the income gain starts
rows.explainer: Not used: no income gain is counted here (above).

rows.label: Years the long-term income gain lasts
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for how long a long-term income gain lasts (GiveWell's working years, 40), read by every model that counts one (INV-13).

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate, the wait included, so the result moves with it. Never type in a present value worked out elsewhere: rebuild it from its inputs.

rows.label: Resource sharing within households (multiplier on an earner's gain)
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's): an earner's income gain is shared with the household, so it counts this many times. Read by every model that values a long-term income gain (INV-13).

rows.label: Internal validity of the trials, a multiplier
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.9 (0.75 to 1): the review rates the mortality evidence moderate certainty, downgraded for unclear allocation concealment and unblinded assessment, with no heterogeneity (I² 0%) across 14 trials; a fixed-effect pool of small trials with a wide interval earns a modest cut.

rows.label: External validity: the trials' setting against this program's, a multiplier
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.9 (0.7 to 1.1). Against: First Embrace's newborns get less skin-to-skin than most trials' (3.6 hours a day on average in the first months, its six-month update firstembrace.org.uk/updates/first6months, against the WHO's 8 or more; only the babies under 2 hours a day are taken out, in implementation_adj), and the hospital is crowded with few incubators. For: about a quarter of its newborns are unstable and in intensive care, and 57% of those born in the hospital start immediately, where the WHO immediate-KMC trial found a further 25% fall in deaths over later KMC; its nurses also escalate sick newborns to intensive care. A relative effect carries to the hospital's higher baseline.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The product of its two parts.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Judgment 90% (75 to 100%): the pilot hospital had no kangaroo care ward before (the baseline cohort was cared for without it), about 5% of eligible newborns in Africa get kangaroo care, and a 2016 survey found 27% of Nigerian hospitals offering any (First Embrace's What we do page). Nigeria's government aims for 95% coverage by 2030, so some of these newborns would have got some kangaroo care within a few years; the baseline already counts what mothers did on their own.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (70 to 100%): First Embrace pays its own nurses, wraps and feeding equipment, training and monitoring. The hospital gives the ward space and beds and its own staff's time on the extra care (conventional care is in both arms of the trials, so only the kangaroo-care work counts); the Kano State Ministry of Health supervises, and a community programme of eHealth Africa and Dimagi follows up referred newborns.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity, compliance, follow-through)
rows.explainer: 80%: the newborns who get at least 2 hours of skin-to-skin a day, the rate the charity's own model gives for its first year (its pilot report excludes the other 20%: 'We exclude newborns who received less than this (20%) from our reach'; its '730 (960 x 80%)' doesn't multiply out, 960 x 80% being 768). In the review's 2016 version the trials with under 2 hours a day showed no fall in deaths, so the rest count nothing (they are often referred elsewhere or in intensive care). Range 60% to 90%: the share is from the first months, and dose rose about 40% over the pilot.

source.title: First Embrace, reach and cost model (its own sheet, linked from its 2027 funding-gap post)
source.quote: Effective Kangaroo care rate (adherence over 2 hours a day) 80.0%

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Judgment 1 (0.9 to 1.05): no government or other funder pays for kangaroo care at these hospitals, and First Embrace's 2027 budget is half unfunded ($605,000 of $1.2m raised, its funding-gap post), so a donation isn't replacing money that would come anyway. The low end allows for its incubator or other funders filling a gap.

rows.label: Years a donation waits before the charity spends it

source.title: First Embrace, reach and cost model (its own sheet, linked from its 2027 funding-gap post)

rows.explainer: Unspent funds over yearly spending: $236,000 in the bank in late October 2026 against $27,695 a month, about 0.7 years. The low end is the pace of the 2027 budget ($1.2m a year, its funding-gap post), at which the same cash lasts about two months.

rows.label: Years from the charity's spending to the intervention reaching people
rows.explainer: Judgment about five weeks (0 to 3 months): a new hospital needs a week's nurse training and a ward set up; First Embrace launched its first within four months of incubation, approvals included.

rows.label: Years from delivery to the middle of the protection
rows.explainer: Judgment two weeks (0.04 years; a few days to a month): the deaths averted fall within the 28-day neonatal period, so the benefit is discounted from its middle.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the benefits come
rows.explainer: Every wait is discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit (the income gain's own wait is counted from delivery, in ln_income_gain_per_person).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: 1, measured: the charity's own count of newborns enrolled (nurses' session logs, followed to day 28) meets an effect from randomised trials of the same intervention delivered the same way, kangaroo care for small newborns on a hospital ward, in the shared Cochrane review across the durations hospitals achieve. How far it carries is in evidence_adj; the low dose in implementation_adj.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Treatment costs averted, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: 0: kangaroo care doesn't shorten hospital stays (the 2026 Cochrane review found stays about a day longer), and First Embrace delays discharge of the smallest newborns.

rows.label: Rebound malaria from lost immunity, as a share of value lost
rows.explainer: 0: only malaria prevention has this effect.

rows.label: Investment of income increases, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: 0: no income gain is modelled.

rows.label: Survivors' later development, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for kangaroo care (facts/newborn_care.json, GiveWell's): growth, breastfeeding and long-run development of the newborns who live.

rows.label: Sick newborns escalated to intensive care by First Embrace's nurses, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: Judgment +3% (0 to +8%): about a quarter of enrolled newborns are unstable and in intensive care (its pilot report, 26%), and the nurses escalate those who deteriorate on the ward, which First Embrace calls significant but unquantified. The trials' conventional-care arms had escalation too, so only what the hospital would have missed counts, a small part.

rows.label: Kangaroo care in hospitals First Embrace never runs, through its work with the state, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: Judgment +3% (0 to +15%): First Embrace shares all its data with the Kano State Ministry of Health and works with it towards the national target of 95% coverage by 2030, its route to scale. Earlier Nigerian programmes it names (ACCESS, MNCH2, PRRINN-MNCH) set kangaroo-care policy without it reaching scale, so the chance that this year's work brings a funded state programme is small; the high end is a state budget line within a few years.

rows.label: Other benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: -2% (-5 to 0%): harms not modelled. Kangaroo care keeps mothers in hospital about a day longer (the 2026 Cochrane review), and First Embrace delays discharge of the smallest newborns, costing families time and money and crowding the wards.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.formula: treatment_costs_share + rebound_share + investment_of_income_share + developmental_share + escalation_share + government_scale_share + other_unmodelled_share
rows.explainer: GiveWell-style supplementary adjustments, each its own row, summed: they add to the modelled value as one share, as in GiveWell's sheets.

rows.label: Deaths averted
Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weight for a death in the first 28 days of life (@moral_weights.givewell_neonatal), times your multiplier on the value of a life: the site's one value of a neonatal death (docs/normalization.md 2.7).

rows.label: Units of value from deaths averted
Units of value from stillbirths averted
rows.explainer: A stillbirth averted at the site's one value (@givewell_shared.uov_per_stillbirth, GiveWell's), times your multiplier on the value of a life.

rows.label: Units of value from later-life income
Units of value from illness averted
rows.explainer: A share of the deaths' and income's value, the base GiveWell's supplementary share has.

rows.label: Illness averted per person reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: 0: illness is counted as a share of the deaths' value (morbidity_value_ratio), not here, so it isn't counted twice.

rows.label: Illness averted, in DALYs
Illness averted, in units of value
rows.explainer: The bridge from DALYs into units of value: the unit's conversion cancels it, so illness counts as healthy years whatever "Healthy year vs doubled-income year" is set to.

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.explainer: Illness and the other supplementary shares add to the modelled value side by side, as one sum of shares does in GiveWell's sheets; illness counted in DALYs comes in through its bridge, inside the side-effect share like every other outcome.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: First Embrace's own share (Convention 1): its two co-directors at $55,000 each and $49,560 of programme team and nurse pay (pilot report, 4.3), $159,560 of the year's $189,720. Range 75% to 90%: the pilot report's 'core team salaries, travel and indirect costs' line mixes pay with other costs.

source.title: First Embrace, reach and cost model (its own sheet, linked from its 2027 funding-gap post)
source.quote: Co-Executive Director salary (per year) $55,000 ... Co-Executive Directors (number) 2

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared gap for delivery staff hired locally (@staff_pay.gap_local_delivery): most of the pay is the Nigerian nurses' (250,000 naira a month, against about 280,000 at a standard hospital in its reach and cost model).

Share of the full cost paid by cash donations
